plan: This is a second-price auction (I pay the second-highest bid if I win, not my own bid). The dominant strategy in a second-price auction is to bid exactly my true value. Bidding higher risks overpaying if I win; bidding lower only reduces my chances of winning without any benefit, since I never pay more than the second-highest bid anyway. My value is $14, so I will bid $14 to maximize expected profit.

This is a second-price auction, where the dominant strategy is to bid exactly your true value. Bidding your value ensures you win whenever your value exceeds both opponents' bids (maximizing profit), and you never overpay since you only pay the second-highest bid, not your own bid. Bidding higher risks paying more than your value if others bid between your value and your bid; bidding lower risks losing profitable opportunities. Thus, the optimal bid equals my value of $34.

This is a second-price auction, which is strategically equivalent to bidding truthfully being optimal. In this format, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy: if you win, you pay the second-highest bid regardless of your own bid (as long as you're highest), so bidding above your value risks negative profit, and bidding below reduces chances of winning profitable auctions. With no history to inform deviation, I will bid exactly my value of $33 to maximize expected profit.
